data.content:
---
name: sdlc-harness
description: |
  Governs work item quality throughout the SDLC for a GitLab project. Onboards to the
  team's workflow, applies best-practice templates, monitors work items, drafts acceptance
  criteria, flags ambiguous descriptions, suggests dependency links, and proposes state
  transitions. Use when the user asks to govern, audit, or improve their backlog or work
  items on the local GitLab demo instance.
---

# SDLC Harness Skill

You are an SDLC governance agent. When invoked, follow this workflow.

## When this skill activates

- The user wants to onboard a project management tool to sdlc-harness.
- The user asks the skill to check, review, or improve one or more work items.
- An agent has produced a suggestion and the user wants to review, approve, edit, or
  reject it.
- The user asks about backlog quality, acceptance criteria, ambiguity, dependencies,
  state transitions, or test coverage linkage.

---

## Scope

This skill acts **only** on the project management project/group established
during onboarding (Phase 1). It never reads or writes issues, merge requests,
or labels in any other GitLab group or project on the same instance, even when
scanning for dependency overlap (Task 22) or monitoring state (Task 23). If the
user wants to govern a different project, they must re-run onboarding to
reconfigure scope — the skill does not infer or expand scope on its own.

---

## Phase 1 — Onboarding (Task 18)

Check whether the project has already been onboarded by looking for a `.sdlc-harness.json`
config in the repo root.

- **Not onboarded:** Run the onboarding conversation below.
- **Already onboarded:** Load the config and proceed to Phase 3.

### Onboarding conversation

Ask the user:

1. Which GitLab project should be governed? (default: `http://localhost:8080/sdlc-harness/weather-dashboard`)
2. What work item types does the team use? (e.g. Story, Bug, Task, Epic)
3. What are the workflow states? (e.g. Open, In Progress, In Review, Done)
4. What are the valid state transitions? (e.g. Open → In Progress, In Progress → In Review)
5. Are there existing work item templates to follow?

Save answers to `.sdlc-harness.json` in the repo root using the `ProjectConfig` schema
defined in `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/models.ts`.

---

## Phase 2 — Work Item Templates (Task 19)

<!-- TODO Task 19: Industry best-practice templates for:
     - User Story  (title convention, description structure, Given-When-Then AC)
     - Bug         (steps to reproduce, expected vs actual, severity)
     - Task        (definition of done, effort estimate placeholder)
     - Epic        (goal, child story links, success metrics)
     DELEGATE, DO NOT DUPLICATE: the canonical standard lives in the
     `work-item-format` MCP tool (Task 13). This phase should call
     that tool for title/description/AC structure rather than re-defining the
     standard inline here.
-->

The standard lives in the `work-item-format` MCP tool, not here. Tasks 20 and 21 call
`get-template` at drafting time (see Phase 3), so the template is fetched per work-item
type rather than duplicated in this file or in the agent code.

---

## Phase 3 — Agent Monitoring (Tasks 20–24)

Agents run on demand (user triggers an Audit or a targeted action) and produce
`AgentFinding` or `DependencyFinding` objects (see `src/models.ts`). Each finding
is surfaced for human review (Phase 4) before any write occurs.

### Governance action menu

When the user asks to govern issues, present these options:

- **Audit** — run all P0 agents across all open issues and compile a report
- **Draft AC** — run the AC agent on a specific issue or all issues missing AC
- **Check ambiguity** — run the ambiguity agent on a specific issue or all issues
- **Suggest links** — run the dependency agent across all open issues
- **Check transitions** — run the state-transition agent across all open issues
- **Coverage** — run the test coverage agent (only if `coverage.enabled` is true in config)

---

## Agents

| ID | Agent | Concern |
|---|---|---|
| AC | Acceptance-criteria | Issues without Given-When-Then AC |
| AM | Ambiguity detection | Issues with vague or contradictory descriptions |
| DEP | Dependency suggestion | Issues that likely block or relate to each other |
| ST | State-transition | Issues whose GitLab state is stale relative to activity |
| TC *(P1)* | Test-coverage linkage | Issues with no linked test file or test-plan item |

TC is disabled by default (seed data has no test files). To enable:
1. Add at least one test file to `weather-app/` (e.g. `weather.test.js`).
2. Set `"testGlob": "weather-app/**/*.test.*"` in `.sdlc-harness.json`.
3. TC will be included in subsequent audit runs automatically.

---

### Acceptance Criteria Agent (Task 20)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/ac-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runAcAgent(issue, config) → AgentFinding | null`

The agent finds the issues that need criteria. **You write the criteria.** It returns a
`draft` brief, never finished prose — `suggestedValue` holds a placeholder, and
`applyFinding` throws if you try to apply a finding that still carries a brief.

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Call `runAcAgent(issue, projectConfig)` for each issue in scope.
2. `null` means the issue already has usable criteria. Skip it silently.
3. Otherwise you get a finding with `draft: { task, context, unknowns }`:
   - Call `work-item-format` with `action: "get-template"` and
     `type: draft.context.workItemType`, and follow the structure it returns. That tool is
     the single source of truth for format — do not invent your own layout here.
   - Write 2–4 Given-When-Then criteria grounded in `draft.context.title` and
     `draft.context.description`. Cover the main path and at least one failure case.
   - If `draft.unknowns` is non-empty, those are gaps the issue does not fill. Put a
     direct question to the author in place of each gap. Do not choose a plausible value.
   - Replace `suggestedValue` with what you wrote, delete the `draft` field, then take the
     finding to Phase 4.

**Write criteria that could only belong to this issue.** Anything that would read the same
on an unrelated ticket is filler and should be rewritten — "the system responds correctly",
"the change takes effect and is visible in the UI", "no data is corrupted". If the issue
genuinely does not say enough to write a specific criterion, ask; a question is more useful
to the author than a sentence that asserts nothing.

**Detection rules (deterministic, no model needed):** returns `null` when the description
contains an "Acceptance Criteria" heading, `## AC`, `## Criteria`, or structured
Given/When/Then where each clause opens its own line. Three keywords in one line of prose
does not count.

**Tool calls:** `gitlab-issue-reader` to fetch issues, `work-item-format` for the template.
Never call `gitlab-issue-writer` directly — writes go through the review interface.

---

### Ambiguity Detection Agent (Task 21)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/ambiguity-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runAmbiguityAgent(issue, config) → AgentFinding | null`

Same split as Task 20: the agent locates the vague wording, **you write the replacement.**
The finding carries a `draft` brief and a placeholder `suggestedValue`.

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Call `runAmbiguityAgent(issue, projectConfig)` for each issue in scope.
2. `null` means the description is already specific. Do not flag it.
3. Otherwise:
   - `draft.context.flaggedPhrases` lists the exact spans that cannot be tested against.
     Replace each one. Leave the rest of the description alone.
   - `draft.context.reusableDetail` holds concrete material already in the issue — file
     paths, code references, error names. Prefer these over anything you supply yourself.
   - `draft.unknowns` lists flagged phrases with no replacement available in the issue.
     Write a question to the author in place of each. Never fill one with a guess.
   - Replace `suggestedValue` with the rewritten description, delete `draft`, then take the
     finding to Phase 4.

**This replaces the author's text, so keep their voice.** Rewrite what is vague and nothing
else. Do not expand a two-line bug report into a templated form with headings they did not
ask for, and do not add scope the author never mentioned. The result should read like the
same person wrote it on a better day.

Approving an AM finding **writes to the issue description**. That is deliberate — a rewrite
nobody can apply is not governance.

**False-positive avoidance:** returns `null` when a description is at least 80 characters
and carries two or more specificity signals (file paths, inline code, URLs, API/endpoint/
component/class/function references).

**Detected patterns:** placeholders (TBD/TODO/FIXME/XXX), non-specific pronouns
("the thing", "something", "somehow"), vague subjects ("fix it", "it doesn't work"),
non-testable claims ("does not work"), vague quantities ("various", "several things").
"properly" and "correctly" are deliberately absent — the AC agent's old template used them,
and flagging its output created a loop between the two agents.

**Tool calls:** `gitlab-issue-reader` to fetch issues. Never writes directly.

---

### Dependency Suggestion Agent (Task 22)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/dependency-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runDependencyAgent(issues, config) → DependencyFinding[]`

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Fetch all open issues via `gitlab-issue-reader` (action: `list-issues`, state: `opened`).
2. Call `runDependencyAgent(issues, projectConfig)`.
3. For each `DependencyFinding` returned:
   - Fields: `sourceIid`, `targetIid`, `suggestedLinkType` (`blocks` | `relates-to`),
     `reason`, `confidence` (0–1).
   - Proceed to Phase 4 for each finding.
4. Guarantees: no self-links, no duplicate pairs, confidence in [0,1].

**Overlap detection:** Jaccard similarity on significant keyword tokens (stop-words
removed). Threshold: 0.12 for a finding; 0.25 for high-confidence boost.

**Link type and direction:**
- `blocks` — only when exactly one side carries dependency language ("depends on",
  "requires", "prerequisite", "blocks"). The side that depends on the other is the
  target; the prerequisite side is the source.
- `relates-to` — when both or neither sides carry dependency language (direction is
  ambiguous). The lower IID is always set as `sourceIid` for canonical ordering.
- Domain-specific heuristics (e.g. matching "/token refresh/") are intentionally
  excluded from `BLOCKS_SIGNALS`; they produce unreliable directions on real backlogs.

**Report-only (no write path):** `DependencyFinding` objects are **always report-only**.
The `gitlab-issue-writer` MCP tool has no native issue-links endpoint, so
`applyFinding` never writes for DEP findings (`gitlabWriteCalled` is always `false`).
Present the finding as a recommendation the team can action manually, or document it
as a comment by calling `gitlab-issue-writer` (action: `add-note`) outside the normal
review loop if the user explicitly requests it.

---

### State Transition Agent (Task 23)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/state-transition-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runStateTransitionAgent(issue, mrs, config) → AgentFinding | null`

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. For each open issue, fetch related MRs via `gitlab-mr-reader-writer` (action: `list-mrs`).
   Match MRs by checking their `description` for `Closes #<iid>`, `Fixes #<iid>`, or the
   issue IID appearing in the MR title. Pass the matched MRs as the `mrs` parameter.
2. Call `runStateTransitionAgent(issue, mrs, projectConfig)`.
3. If the return value is `null`, skip — no transition warranted.
4. If the return value is an `AgentFinding` with `agent: 'ST'`:
   - The `suggestedValue` is the target state name (e.g. `'In Review'`).
   - Proceed to Phase 4.

**Signal mapping:**
- MR `state: 'merged'` → propose `'In Review'` (transitively reachable).
- MR `state: 'opened'` → propose `'In Progress'` (if valid from current state).
- No linked MRs → `null`.

**Transition validation:** Uses BFS over `config.transitionRules` to check transitive
reachability. A transition is only proposed if the target state is reachable from the
current state (directly or through intermediate states).

**NEVER automatically changes GitLab state.** All proposals go through Phase 4.

**Write path (if user accepts):** Call `gitlab-issue-writer` (action: `update-issue`)
with the appropriate `state_event` (`close` for Done, otherwise update labels to reflect
the new state).

---

### Test Coverage Linkage Agent (Task 24 — P1 stretch, disabled by default)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/agents/coverage-agent.ts`
**Export:** `runCoverageAgent(issues, testContents, config) → AgentFinding[]`

**Enabled only when** `config.coverage.enabled === true` in the project config.
Add `"coverage": { "testFilePatterns": ["**/*.test.ts"], "enabled": true }` to
`.sdlc-harness.json` to enable.

**Runtime behaviour:**

1. Read test file contents matching the configured glob patterns.
2. Call `runCoverageAgent(issues, testContents, projectConfig)`.
3. Issues with no `#<iid>` or `closes #<iid>` reference in any test file are flagged.
4. Surface each finding through Phase 4.

---

## Phase 4 — Human Review Interface (Task 25)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/skill/review.ts`
**Exports:** `applyFinding(finding, options, adapter?)`, `rejectFinding(finding)`

### Review presentation

For each `AgentFinding` or `DependencyFinding`, present to the user:

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔍 [AGENT-TAG] Issue #<iid>: <issue title>
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Reason: <finding.reason>

Proposed change:
<finding.suggestedValue>
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Reply with:
  apply     — accept and write to GitLab
  edit <…>  — accept with your changes and write
  skip      — move on without logging
  reject    — discard and log rejection
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

### Decision handling

| User input | Action | Logged |
|------------|--------|--------|
| `apply` | Call `applyFinding(finding, { editedValue: null })` | ✓ `accepted` |
| `edit <text>` | Call `applyFinding(finding, { editedValue: '<text>' })` | ✓ `edited` |
| `skip` | No-op | ✗ not logged |
| `reject` | Call `rejectFinding(finding)` | ✓ `rejected` |

**Only `apply` and `edit` call the GitLab writer adapter.** `skip` and `reject` do not
modify any GitLab data.

### Conflict Detection

A conflict arises when two agents produce suggestions that contradict each other on the same
issue. The two most common cases:

- DEP suggests issue A *blocks* issue B (implying A must finish first), while ST suggests
  transitioning A to Done (implying it is already complete).
- AM rewrites a description in a way that would invalidate AC drafted by AC in the same run.

Before presenting the review, check for overlapping `issueIid` values across all agent
findings. Conflicting findings are grouped and flagged:

```
⚡ CONFLICT — Issue #7 has suggestions from two agents that may contradict:

  [ST] Proposed transition: Open → In Progress
       (reason: MR !3 referencing this issue was opened 2h ago)

  [DEP] Proposed link: #7 blocks #9
       (reason: both issues describe the same auth token refresh logic)

  → apply ST first / apply DEP first / apply both / skip both
```

Do not auto-resolve conflicts. The user decides.

When multiple agents produce findings for the **same issue IID** in the same session,
surface them one at a time in a numbered list before presenting each individually:

```
⚠️  Multiple findings for issue #<iid>:
  1. [AC]  Draft missing acceptance criteria
  2. [AM]  Rewrite vague description

Review them in order. Apply, edit, skip, or reject each separately.
```

After the user handles all findings for an issue, proceed to the next issue.

### Writer adapter contract

At runtime, `applyFinding` calls the adapter only for **writable actions**.
The `defaultWriterAdapter` (in `gitlab-writer-adapter.ts`) deliberately returns
`written: false` when no real adapter is injected, so telemetry will never record
`outcome: accepted` for writes that never reached GitLab.  Pass `stubWriterAdapter`
explicitly in unit tests.

Action-specific write semantics (for a real adapter):

| `action` | Write operation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `draft_ac` | Append drafted AC to issue description | `update-issue`; refused while the finding still carries a `draft` |
| `state_transition` | Apply scoped label swap; GitLab has only `opened`/`closed` states | `update-issue` |
| `rewrite_desc` | Replace issue description with the drafted rewrite | `update-issue`; refused while the finding still carries a `draft` |
| `missing_coverage` | **Never written** — report only | COV findings are informational |
| `dependency_link` | **Never written** by the adapter — report only | No links API; use `add-note` outside review loop if needed |

**Missing integration note:** The `gitlab-issue-writer` MCP tool does not yet expose a
native "add link" operation. Until it does, dependency links are presented as
recommendations only.  The adapter boundary in `gitlab-writer-adapter.ts` is the
documented extension point for a future real integration.

---

## Phase 5 — Suggestion Telemetry (Task 26)

**Module:** `bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/src/skill/telemetry.ts`
**File:** `sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl` (in the working directory; gitignored)

### Logged events

One JSON object is appended per **accepted**, **edited**, or **rejected** decision.
**Skip is neutral and NOT logged.**

**Schema (one object per line):**
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2025-09-01T10:00:00.000Z",
  "agent": "AC",
  "issueIid": 12,
  "action": "draft_ac",
  "outcome": "accepted",
  "editedFields": []
}
```

**Security rules:**
- Never log issue title, description, or any GitLab content.
- Never log credentials, tokens, or URLs containing auth params.
- The file is append-only; existing entries are never modified.
- The file is gitignored (`sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl`).

### Telemetry

Every apply / edit / reject outcome is appended to `sdlc-harness-telemetry.jsonl` in the
repo root (append-only, never overwritten). The file is gitignored and contains no issue
content — only metadata.

```jsonc
{
  "ts": "2025-09-01T14:32:10Z",
  "agent": "AC",
  "issueIid": 12,
  "action": "draft_ac",
  "outcome": "accepted",   // "accepted" | "edited" | "rejected" | "failed"
  "editedFields": []       // populated when outcome = "edited"
}
```

The acceptance rate (`accepted / (accepted + rejected)`) is the primary trust metric for the demo.
Note: `"failed"` outcomes (write attempted but adapter returned `written: false`) are excluded
from both the numerator and denominator of all rate calculations.

### Acceptance-rate summary

Call `computeAcceptanceRate(entries)` from `telemetry.ts` to get:

```
Total:           N decisions logged (failed excluded)
Accepted:        N  (N%)
Edited:          N  (N%)
Rejected:        N  (N%)
Failed:          N  (write did not reach GitLab — excluded from rates)
Acceptance rate: N%     (accepted / total)
Approval rate:   N%     (accepted + edited) / total
```

Present this summary when the user asks "how are we doing?" or at the end of an Audit.

### Environment override

Set `SDLC_TELEMETRY_PATH` env var to redirect the telemetry file (used in tests).

---

## MCP Tools available to this skill

The following MCP tools are registered by the sdlc-harness GitLab MCP server (Section 2A).
Use them when calling GitLab on the user's behalf:

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `gitlab-issue-reader` | Read issues, labels, and current state |
| `gitlab-issue-writer` | Create / update issues, add notes, change state |
| `gitlab-mr-reader-writer` | Read MRs (state-transition signal), write MR notes |
| `work-item-format` | Canonical formatting standard for titles, descriptions, AC |

_Tools are not available until the MCP server (Tasks 7–16) is running and registered (Task 29)._

53 | - **Loading state** — A brief spinner simulates an async data fetch (300 ms).
54 | - **Light / Dark theme** — Toggle button in the header; selection is persisted in
55 |   `localStorage` across page reloads.
56 | - **Accessible** — Semantic HTML, ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and visible focus
57 |   indicators throughout.

1 | # GitLab Local
2 | 
3 | Runs a self-hosted GitLab CE instance and a static demo site locally via Docker,
4 | with a reproducible demo environment.
5 | 
6 | ## Requirements
7 | 
8 | - Docker
9 | - Docker Compose v2+
10 | - Bash 3.2+
11 | - curl
12 | - Python 3 (used for portable base64, URL encoding, and JSON encoding)
13 | 
14 | ### Minimum host requirements
15 | 
16 | | Resource | Minimum | Recommended |
17 | |---|---|---|
18 | | RAM | 4 GB free | 8 GB free |
19 | | CPU | 2 cores | 4 cores |
20 | | Disk | 10 GB free | 20 GB free |
21 | 
22 | `docker-compose.yml` is already tuned down for local/demo use (`puma['worker_processes'] = 2`,
23 | `sidekiq['concurrency'] = 5`, `prometheus_monitoring['enable'] = false`) — GitLab CE's own
24 | [hardware requirements](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/install/requirements.html) recommend 8 GB+ for
25 | a comfortable experience, but this configuration has been run successfully at the 4 GB minimum for
26 | demo purposes. If you're on Docker Desktop (Windows/Mac), make sure its own VM resource limits
27 | (Settings → Resources) are set at or above these values — the container can't use more memory or
28 | CPU than Docker Desktop itself is allowed.
29 | 
30 | ## Quick Start
31 | 
32 | ```bash
33 | cd gitlab-local
34 | 
35 | # 1. Create your local credentials file with owner-only permissions
36 | install -m 600 .env.example .env
37 | #    Replace both GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD and GITLAB_DEMO_PASSWORD placeholders
38 | 
39 | # 2. Start the stack, wait until healthy, and run the complete idempotent seed
40 | ./manage.sh start
41 | 
42 | # 3. Create/refresh the API token used by the MCP server and live tests
43 | ./manage.sh refresh-token
44 | ```
45 | 
46 | If `install` is unavailable, run `umask 077` before copying `.env.example`.
47 | 
48 | Then open **http://localhost:8080** (GitLab) and **http://localhost:8081** (demo site).
49 | 
50 | ## Credentials
51 | 
52 | Credentials come from your local `.env` file. Both values are explicit, must
53 | contain at least eight characters, and must differ. The seed workflow rejects
54 | placeholder or identical values.
55 | 
56 | | Account    | Username | Role      |
57 | |------------|----------|-----------|
58 | | Admin      | `root`   | Owner     |
59 | | Demo user  | `demo`   | Developer |
60 | 
61 | The accounts use separate settings:
62 | 
63 | - `GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD` configures the initial GitLab administrator password.
64 | - `GITLAB_DEMO_PASSWORD` configures the non-admin demo account.
65 | 
66 | `seed.sh` does not silently reuse the administrator password. On normal reruns, it
67 | synchronizes the existing demo account to `GITLAB_DEMO_PASSWORD`. When an administrator
68 | `GITLAB_TOKEN` is supplied to avoid Rails startup, the existing password is left unchanged.
69 | 
70 | Base provisioning also repairs the demo account on every run: it restores a usable
71 | account state and adds or corrects its group membership to Developer access.
72 | 
73 | > **Sign in with `root` or `demo`. Do not use "Register now".**
74 | > `seed.sh` sets `signup_enabled=false` — this is a closed demo instance. If you
75 | > register an account anyway, GitLab creates it in a blocked state and you get
76 | > *"Your account is pending approval from your GitLab administrator and hence
77 | > blocked."* That is expected. Sign in as `root` instead; the blocked account can
78 | > be ignored, or removed from **Admin → Users**.
79 | 
80 | Passwords are deliberately not emitted by the seed scripts. Retrieve them from
81 | the local password store or `.env` without placing them in logs or screen captures.
82 | 
83 | On POSIX systems, every helper script refuses to continue when `.env` grants
84 | group/world permissions. Repair an existing file with `chmod 600 .env`. Git Bash on
85 | Windows skips the POSIX mode check because Windows ACLs are authoritative there;
86 | restrict the file to your Windows account instead.
87 | 
88 | ## Demo Project
89 | 
90 | After seeding, the demo project is at:
91 | 
92 | **http://localhost:8080/sdlc-harness/weather-dashboard**
93 | 
94 | It contains the **Weather Dashboard** — a self-contained mock weather app built as the
95 | SDLC Harness demo artefact (sourced from the `dev` branch of the sdlc-harness repo):
96 | 
97 | | File | Description |
98 | |---|---|
99 | | `index.html` | App shell — open directly in any browser, no server needed |
100 | | `styles.css` | All styling — dark mode, responsive, CSS custom properties |
101 | | `app.js` | Runtime behaviour — mock data, search, theme toggle |
102 | | `WEATHER-DASHBOARD.md` | Full docs + suggested SDLC demo changes |
103 | | `tests.md` | Manual test checklist |
104 | 
105 | ## Helper Scripts
106 | 
107 | | Command                       | Description                                           |
108 | |-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
109 | | `./smoke.sh`                  | Validate full stack health on demand (exit 0 = OK); run automatically by `start`, `restart`, and `reset` |
110 | | `./manage.sh start`           | Start, wait until healthy, and run the complete seed  |
111 | | `./manage.sh stop`            | Stop the stack                                        |
112 | | `./manage.sh restart`         | Restart, wait until healthy, and run the complete seed|
113 | | `./manage.sh seed`            | Run the complete idempotent demo seed                  |
114 | | `./manage.sh refresh-token`   | Rotate and verify the gitignored MCP/API token         |
115 | | `./manage.sh reset [-y]`      | Full wipe + fresh boot + reseed in one command (see Full Reset below) |
116 | | `./manage.sh uninstall [-y]`  | Remove the stack, generated state, and Bob/MCP installation |
117 | | `./manage.sh password`        | Show GitLab's temporary initial root password, if available |
118 | | `./manage.sh logs`            | Tail container logs                                   |
119 | | `./manage.sh status`          | Show container health                                 |
120 | 
121 | `./manage.sh seed` is the only public seeding operation. It keeps the implementation
122 | modular by invoking `seed.sh` for base provisioning and then `seed-issues.sh` for
123 | scenario fixtures. The complete workflow is **idempotent**, and the issue stage converges its
124 | state-transition fixture to two open issues linked from a genuinely merged MR with a real
125 | branch commit.
126 | 
127 | Unless the caller supplies `GITLAB_TOKEN`, `seed.sh` creates one one-day Rails PAT and
128 | shares it with the internal issue-fixture stage. It keeps the token in owner-only temporary
129 | files and revokes it from an EXIT cleanup path. Successful completion includes PAT
130 | revocation and removal of container-side token files.
131 | 
132 | ## Ports
133 | 
134 | | Port | Purpose |
135 | |---|---|
136 | | 8080 | GitLab web UI / API (host to container nginx port 80) |
137 | | 8081 | Demo site (nginx); override with `DEMO_SITE_PORT` |
138 | | 2222 | Git over SSH |
139 | 
140 | All published ports bind to `127.0.0.1`; they are not exposed on other host
141 | interfaces. GitLab's external URL is `http://localhost:8080`, so generated web
142 | and clone URLs retain the required `:8080` port.
143 | 
144 | SSH remote URL format:
145 | ```
146 | ssh://git@localhost:2222/<namespace>/<repo>.git
147 | ```
148 | 
149 | ## Troubleshooting
150 | 
151 | ### "Your account is pending approval from your GitLab administrator"
152 | 
153 | You registered a new account instead of signing in. This is a closed instance —
154 | sign in as `root` (see [Credentials](#credentials)). Nothing is broken.
155 | 
156 | ### `./smoke.sh` reports the demo site is not up
157 | 
158 | The nginx demo site did not bind its port. This is usually a port collision — on
159 | macOS, Docker Desktop's own helper process binds 8081 on some installs, so the
160 | container exits immediately and never appears in `docker compose ps`.
161 | 
162 | ```bash
163 | lsof -iTCP:8081 -sTCP:LISTEN     # find what holds the port
164 | ```
165 | 
166 | Then pick a free port in `.env` and bring the stack back up:
167 | 
168 | ```bash
169 | echo "DEMO_SITE_PORT=8082" >> .env
170 | docker compose up -d
171 | ```
172 | 
173 | `smoke.sh` requires GitLab's host-facing sign-in page, GitLab's internal readiness probe,
174 | and the demo site to pass. A missing or partially initialized service produces a non-zero
175 | result.
176 | 
177 | ### Seeding hangs at "Creating API token..."
178 | 
179 | Without a caller-supplied token, the seed workflow mints one token by booting GitLab's
180 | Rails environment inside the container (`gitlab-rails runner`). That boot is the heaviest
181 | step and can stall on a long-running or resource-constrained instance. It is now bounded
182 | to 180 seconds (override with `GITLAB_RAILS_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) and exits with an
183 | actionable error instead of hanging indefinitely.
184 | 
185 | Skip it by supplying an administrator token. In GitLab (signed in as `root`) go to
186 | **User settings → Access tokens**, create one with the `api` scope, then:
187 | 
188 | ```bash
189 | export GITLAB_TOKEN=[REDACTED]
190 | ./manage.sh seed
191 | ```
192 | 
193 | The public seed operation validates that the token belongs to an administrator and passes
194 | it to the internal issue-fixture stage. This path does not start Rails and is the most
195 | reliable option for an already-provisioned demo instance.
196 | 
197 | `./manage.sh refresh-token` serves a different purpose: it rotates the non-admin demo
198 | user token used by Bob's MCP integration. That token cannot perform the administrator
199 | operations required by the seed workflow.
200 | 
201 | To refresh the MCP token, run:
202 | 
203 | ```bash
204 | ./manage.sh refresh-token
205 | ```
206 | 
207 | It rotates a 30-day API token for the `demo` user, stores it in the repository
208 | root `.env` with mode `600`, verifies authentication, and never prints the token.
209 | 
210 | If seeding is genuinely slow rather than stuck, check Docker Desktop's memory
211 | allocation — GitLab CE wants 4 GB and will thrash below that.
212 | 
213 | ---
214 | 
215 | ### The password in `.env` does not work
216 | 
217 | GitLab enforces a minimum of eight characters. For values containing `$`, keep
218 | the value single-quoted in `.env` so Docker Compose treats it literally:
219 | 
220 | ```dotenv
221 | GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD=[REDACTED]
222 | GITLAB_DEMO_PASSWORD=[REDACTED]
223 | ```
224 | 
225 | Keep each assignment on one line with no `export` prefix. The scripts parse only
226 | the named `KEY=value` entries and never execute `.env` as shell code.
227 | 
228 | Changing `GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD` does not update an existing root account. Use
229 | GitLab's documented administrator password-reset procedure, or reset this disposable
230 | stack if deleting its data is acceptable:
231 | 
232 | ```bash
233 | ./manage.sh reset -y
234 | ```
235 | 
236 | After changing `GITLAB_DEMO_PASSWORD`, unset `GITLAB_TOKEN` and rerun
237 | `./manage.sh seed`; the Rails-free token path intentionally leaves an existing
238 | demo password unchanged.
239 | 
240 | ### GitLab returns HTTP 502 for the first few minutes
241 | 
242 | Normal. Rails is still booting and compiling assets on first run — allow 3–5
243 | minutes. `smoke.sh` polls for up to 300s.
244 | 
245 | ---
246 | 
247 | ## Data Persistence
248 | 
249 | All GitLab data is stored in named Docker volumes:
250 | 
251 | - `gitlab-config` — `/etc/gitlab`
252 | - `gitlab-logs` — `/var/log/gitlab`
253 | - `gitlab-data` — `/var/opt/gitlab`
254 | 
255 | The GitLab and nginx images are pinned by digest in `docker-compose.yml`. `GITLAB_IMAGE`
256 | can temporarily override the GitLab image during a reviewed upgrade path; leave it unset
257 | for new installations.
258 | 
259 | ## Migrating an Existing Stack
260 | 
261 | Do not point arbitrary existing GitLab volumes at the pinned image. GitLab upgrades and
262 | downgrades are version-sensitive; unsupported jumps can make the database unusable.
263 | 
264 | ### Configuration-only migration
265 | 
266 | Use this path to apply the loopback bindings and `:8080` external URL while keeping the
267 | exact GitLab image currently running:
268 | 
269 | 1. Back up GitLab data, `/etc/gitlab`, and `gitlab-secrets.json` according to
270 |    GitLab's Docker backup documentation. Store copies outside the Docker volumes.
271 | 2. Run `chmod 600 .env`, add an explicit `GITLAB_DEMO_PASSWORD`, and replace
272 |    documented placeholders. Do not expect changing the root value to update the
273 |    persisted root account.
274 | 3. Record the current version with `docker exec gitlab gitlab-rake gitlab:env:info`.
275 | 4. Record and tag the exact running image:
276 | 
277 | ```bash
278 | CURRENT_IMAGE_ID="$(docker inspect --format '{{.Image}}' gitlab)"
279 | docker image tag "$CURRENT_IMAGE_ID" gitlab-local-config-migration:current
280 | ```
281 | 
282 | 5. Set `GITLAB_IMAGE=gitlab-local-config-migration:current` in `.env`, then
283 |    recreate without pulling another GitLab image:
284 | 
285 | ```bash
286 | docker compose up -d --no-deps --pull never gitlab
287 | docker compose up -d --no-deps demo-site
288 | ./smoke.sh
289 | ./manage.sh seed
290 | ```
291 | 
292 | Keep the override until a separate GitLab image upgrade is completed. `restart` alone
293 | does not apply changed Compose environment or port mappings.
294 | 
295 | ### GitLab image upgrade
296 | 
297 | 1. Inspect the running version with `docker exec gitlab gitlab-rake gitlab:env:info`.
298 | 2. Inspect the pinned candidate without attaching volumes:
299 | 
300 | ```bash
301 | docker run --rm --entrypoint cat \
302 |   gitlab/gitlab-ce@sha256:f63df4c43029fe91db370609c0b40a1e3585cebd06e3e9637d93a9a3030eb86e \
303 |   /RELEASE
304 | ```
305 | 
306 | 3. Compare the versions against GitLab's official upgrade-path tool and
307 |    documentation. Do not downgrade, and do not skip required upgrade stops.
308 | 4. Take and verify a fresh application backup plus separate copies of
309 |    `/etc/gitlab` and `gitlab-secrets.json` before the first upgrade and every
310 |    required stop. A backup restores only to the same GitLab version and edition.
311 | 5. Set `GITLAB_IMAGE` to the exact reviewed tag or digest for the next required
312 |    stop, pull that image, and run `docker compose up -d --no-deps gitlab`.
313 | 6. At every stop, wait for GitLab to become healthy and run
314 |    `docker exec gitlab gitlab-rake gitlab:background_migrations:status`. Continue
315 |    only after all batched background migrations finish; resolve any pending
316 |    database migrations or failed health checks.
317 | 7. Repeat one required stop at a time. Only after reaching the pinned version
318 |    should you remove the `GITLAB_IMAGE` override and recreate from the default digest.
319 | 8. Run `./smoke.sh`. Starting or restarting through `manage.sh` automatically
320 |    reconciles the complete seed.
321 | 
322 | Do not use `reset` for either migration path unless deleting all existing GitLab data is
323 | intentional.
324 | 
325 | ## Full Reset
326 | 
327 | To wipe all data and start fresh (e.g. for a clean demo re-take):
328 | 
329 | ```bash
330 | ./manage.sh reset          # prompts for confirmation
331 | ./manage.sh reset -y       # skips the confirmation prompt
332 | ```
333 | 
334 | This tears down the stack including volumes, boots fresh, waits for GitLab's
335 | host-facing HTTP endpoint and internal readiness via `smoke.sh`, runs the complete
336 | seed, and refreshes the repository-root MCP token. Equivalent to running by hand:
337 | 
338 | ```bash
339 | docker compose down -v
340 | docker compose up -d
341 | ./smoke.sh
342 | ./manage.sh seed
343 | ./manage.sh refresh-token
344 | ```
345 | 
346 | After a reset, unset any previously exported `GITLAB_TOKEN` and restart or reconnect Bob;
347 | an already-running MCP process still holds the token from before the volumes were deleted.
348 |

Contents of file README.md:

1 | # sdlc-harness
2 | 
3 | IBM Hackathon project. sdlc-harness is a Bob skill that governs work item quality on a
4 | GitLab backlog throughout the SDLC: it drafts missing acceptance criteria, flags vague
5 | descriptions, suggests dependency links, and proposes state transitions, all surfaced to
6 | a developer for review inside Bob before anything gets written back to GitLab. See
7 | [Problem Statement & Solution](docs/problem-statement.html) for the full problem/solution
8 | writeup and [How Bob Was Used to Build This](docs/bob-usage.html) for how Bob was used to
9 | build this project. Documentation lives under `docs/` as self-contained HTML; start at
10 | [docs/index.html](docs/index.html).
11 | 
12 | The repo is self-contained: a Docker Compose stack runs a real GitLab CE instance plus a
13 | small demo web app ("Weather Dashboard") to govern, and a Bob skill/MCP server pair does
14 | the governance work.
15 | 
16 | ## Repository layout
17 | 
18 | | Directory | What it is |
19 | |---|---|
20 | | `gitlab-local/` | Docker stack (GitLab CE + nginx demo site) and all the scripts to start, seed, and reset it. |
21 | | `weather-app/` | The demo artefact under governance — plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step. |
22 | | `bob-kit/` | Installable source and templates for the Bob skill, MCP server, rules, and mode. See "Installing the Bob skill" below. |
23 | | `docs/` | Project documentation as self-contained HTML (`docs/index.html` is the entry point). |
24 | | `bob-sessions/` | Screenshots of Bob task/session summaries captured during the build, kept for hackathon submission. |
25 | 
26 | ## Running the demo
27 | 
28 | > **Windows users:** run every command below in **Git Bash** (installed with Git for
29 | > Windows), not WSL or PowerShell. If you also have WSL installed, plain `bash` may
30 | > resolve to `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` (the WSL launcher) instead of Git Bash —
31 | > check with `where bash`; Git Bash's path should contain `Program Files\Git`. If it
32 | > resolves to WSL, invoke Git Bash explicitly, e.g.
33 | > `"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe" bob-kit/mcp-server/install.sh`. WSL is a separate
34 | > Linux environment with its own PATH, so tools installed on your Windows host (Node.js,
35 | > Docker Desktop) may appear "not installed" there even when they're present on Windows.
36 | 
37 | 1. Start the GitLab stack:
38 |    ```bash
39 |    install -m 600 gitlab-local/.env.example gitlab-local/.env
40 |    # Set distinct GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD and GITLAB_DEMO_PASSWORD values.
41 |    ./gitlab-local/manage.sh start
42 |    ```
43 |    `start` waits for the host-facing GitLab sign-in page, internal readiness, and the
44 |    demo site, then runs the complete idempotent seed. `restart` performs the same checks
45 |    and seed reconciliation. Use `./gitlab-local/manage.sh seed` to reconcile explicitly.
46 |    Full details, including minimum host requirements and the ports each service uses, are
47 |    in [gitlab-local/README.md](gitlab-local/README.md). To wipe and reseed at any point,
48 |    run `./gitlab-local/manage.sh reset`.
49 | 
50 | 2. Install the Bob skill (one-time, per machine):
51 |    ```bash
52 |    bash bob-kit/mcp-server/install.sh
53 |    ```
54 |    This builds and tests the skill and MCP server, merges the sdlc-harness mode and MCP
55 |    registration without touching unrelated Bob configuration, and runs a smoke test. See
56 |    [bob-kit/README.md](bob-kit/README.md) for the manual steps if you'd rather not run the
57 |    installer.
58 | 
59 |    Bob uses its built-in model; there is no provider or model setup for this skill. The
60 |    skill controls when generation is invoked, not which model runs it. It invokes
61 |    generation for acceptance-criteria and ambiguity prose (and full-audit summarization),
62 |    while dependency, transition, and coverage detection are deterministic.
63 | 
64 | 3. Give the MCP server your GitLab credentials. It's a `stdio` server that Bob spawns
65 |    itself (no separate process to run) — but it exits immediately if these are missing,
66 |    which shows up in Bob as `Disconnected` with no further explanation. Add the following
67 |    to the **repository-root** `.env` (a different file from `gitlab-local/.env` used in
68 |    step 1). Create it with owner-only permissions, or merge these values into an existing
69 |    file and run `chmod 600 .env`:
70 |    ```bash
71 |    install -m 600 bob-kit/mcp-server/.env.example .env
72 |    ```
73 |    ```dotenv
74 |    GITLAB_HOST=http://localhost:8080
75 |    GITLAB_PROJECT=sdlc-harness/weather-dashboard
76 |    GITLAB_TOKEN=[REDACTED] ./gitlab-local/manage.sh refresh-token, or a GitLab PAT>
77 |    ```
78 |    `./gitlab-local/manage.sh refresh-token` can mint, store, and verify the demo user's
79 |    token without displaying it.
80 |    Then restart Bob (or reconnect the `sdlc-harness` server from Bob's MCP settings panel).
81 | 
82 | 4. In Bob, switch to the `🔧 SDLC Harness` mode and say something like `govern my backlog`.
83 |    The skill walks through a short onboarding conversation the first time, then runs the
84 |    agents against the seeded issues. Audits are read-only; each finding then enters an
85 |    apply/edit/skip/reject review loop, and only apply or edit can write through the guarded
86 |    review runtime. The full onboarding runbook is in
87 |    [docs/onboarding/runbook.html](docs/onboarding/runbook.html).
88 | 
89 | ## Maintenance
90 | 
91 | - Rotate the local API token with `./gitlab-local/manage.sh refresh-token`.
92 | - Remove only the installed Bob skill, rule, mode, MCP registration, and build artifacts
93 |   with `bash bob-kit/mcp-server/uninstall.sh`.
94 | - Return the whole demo to a freshly cloned state with
95 |   `./gitlab-local/manage.sh uninstall`; this also deletes Docker volumes, local `.env`
96 |   files, onboarding state, and telemetry, so it prompts before proceeding.
97 | 
98 | ## Security
99 | 
100 | This repo started from IBM's hackathon project template, which ships a few guardrails to
101 | keep credentials out of git history:
102 | 
103 | - `.gitignore` and `.bobignore` exclude every `.env` file and anything that looks like a
104 |   credential, key, or secret by name.
105 | - Each part of the stack that needs credentials has an `.env.example`. Create local
106 |   `.env` files with mode `0600` (`install -m 600 ...`) and never commit them. The GitLab
107 |   root and demo accounts must use separate passwords.
108 | - Before pushing, check `git diff` for anything that shouldn't be there and confirm `.env`
109 |   isn't staged (`git status`).
110 | 
111 | [Security Guidelines](docs/security.html) has the full checklist. If in doubt, ask before
112 | pushing rather than after.
113 |

arguments.title: Add Air Quality Index (AQI) display for searched cities
arguments.description:
## Story Narrative

**As a** weather dashboard user  
**I want to** see the Air Quality Index (AQI) for any city I search  
**So that** I can make informed decisions about outdoor activities based on both weather and air quality

## Background

The dashboard currently shows temperature, humidity, wind speed, and weather condition. Adding a mock AQI value (deterministically derived from the city name, same approach as existing mock data) rounds out the health-related context a user needs at a glance.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** a user searches for any city  
**When** the weather card is displayed  
**Then** the card shows an AQI value between 0 and 300  
**And** the AQI is colour-coded (Good ≤50 green, Moderate 51–100 yellow, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups 101–150 orange, Unhealthy 151–200 red)  
**And** the AQI label text describes the category (e.g. "Good", "Moderate")

**Given** the user is in dark mode  
**When** the AQI badge is rendered  
**Then** the colour coding remains accessible (sufficient contrast against the dark surface)

**Given** a screen-reader user navigates to the weather card  
**When** focus reaches the AQI element  
**Then** the accessible label announces both the numeric value and the category (e.g. "AQI 42 — Good")

## Implementation Notes

- Derive AQI from `hashString()` with a different bit-shift offset (e.g. `(seed >>> 12) % 301`) so it is independent of humidity/wind but still deterministic per city.
- Add a `card-aqi` `<dd>` entry to the existing `card-details` `<dl>` in `index.html`.
- Add `.aqi-badge` styles and four modifier classes (`.aqi-good`, `.aqi-moderate`, `.aqi-usg`, `.aqi-unhealthy`) to `styles.css`.
- No external API — mock data only.

arguments.title: Add Air Quality Index (AQI) display for searched cities
arguments.description:
## Story Narrative

**As a** weather dashboard user  
**I want to** see the Air Quality Index (AQI) for any city I search  
**So that** I can make informed decisions about outdoor activities based on both weather and air quality

## Background

The dashboard currently shows temperature, humidity, wind speed, and weather condition. Adding a mock AQI value (deterministically derived from the city name, same approach as existing mock data) rounds out the health-related context a user needs at a glance.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** a user searches for any city  
**When** the weather card is displayed  
**Then** the card shows an AQI value between 0 and 300  
**And** the AQI is colour-coded (Good ≤50 green, Moderate 51–100 yellow, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups 101–150 orange, Unhealthy 151–200 red)  
**And** the AQI label text describes the category (e.g. "Good", "Moderate")

**Given** the user is in dark mode  
**When** the AQI badge is rendered  
**Then** the colour coding remains accessible (sufficient contrast against the dark surface)

**Given** a screen-reader user navigates to the weather card  
**When** focus reaches the AQI element  
**Then** the accessible label announces both the numeric value and the category (e.g. "AQI 42 — Good")

## Implementation Notes

- Derive AQI from `hashString()` with a different bit-shift offset (e.g. `(seed >>> 12) % 301`) so it is independent of humidity/wind but still deterministic per city.
- Add a `card-aqi` `dd` entry to the existing `card-details` `dl` in `index.html`.
- Add `.aqi-badge` styles and four modifier classes (`.aqi-good`, `.aqi-moderate`, `.aqi-usg`, `.aqi-unhealthy`) to `styles.css`.
- No external API — mock data only.

/**
 * Generate deterministic mock weather data for the given city.
 *
 * @param {string} city  City name as entered by the user.
 * @returns {{city: string, tempF: number, condition: string, humidity: string, wind: string, updatedAt: string}}
 */
function getMockWeather(city) {
  const seed = hashString(city.toLowerCase().trim());

  // Temperature: 20 °F – 100 °F range
  const tempF = 20 + (seed % 81);

  // Pick a condition from the list
  const condition = WEATHER_CONDITIONS[seed % WEATHER_CONDITIONS.length];

  // Humidity: 20 % – 95 %
  // NOTE: >>> not >>. The seed is an unsigned 32-bit value, but `>>` coerces
  // to signed first, so any seed >= 2^31 went negative and produced
  // impossible readings (e.g. London: -3 % humidity, -22 mph wind).
  const humidity = (20 + ((seed >>> 4) % 76)) + '%';

  // Wind speed: 0 – 40 mph
  const wind = ((seed >>> 8) % 41) + ' mph';

  // Current timestamp
  const now = new Date();
  const updatedAt = now.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });

  return {
    city: toTitleCase(city.trim()),
    tempF,
    condition,
    humidity,
    wind,
    updatedAt,
  };
}

task.title: Fixes for MCP Server & Gitlab Tooling
task.firstMessage:
For the task 7-16, got this feedback and fix for the code, work according to that: ### 1. Fix MCP tool registration — P0 blocker

In `src/index.ts`, do not use:

```ts
tool.argsSchema.shape ?? {}
The schemas are z.discriminatedUnion objects and have no .shape, causing every registered MCP tool to expose zero input fields.
Use the current MCP SDK API:
server.registerTool(
  tool.name,
  {
    description: tool.description,
    inputSchema: tool.argsSchema,
  },
  async (args) => {
    const result = await tool.execute(args, context);
    return {
      content: [{ type: "text", text: JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) }],
    };
  },
);
Extract server construction into a testable createServer(context) function. Keep index.ts responsible only for configuration, transport startup, and fatal-error handling.
2. Make configuration merging safe and valid
Update merge-bob-config.mjs:
- Write custom modes to ~/.bob/settings/custom_modes.yaml.
- Parse YAML instead of appending raw text.
- Preserve unrelated settings and modes.
- Upsert only the sdlc-harness mode by slug.
- Use bob-kit/custom_modes.yaml as the source of truth instead of maintaining a second embedded mode definition.
- Preserve all unrelated mcp.json entries.
- If existing JSON or YAML is invalid, exit non-zero without changing the file.
- Write through a temporary file and rename it to avoid partial writes.
- Ensure the MCP server name is consistently sdlc-harness; remove conflicting gitlab-local references.
- Keep repeated execution idempotent.
Add tests using temporary directories; never modify the developer’s real ~/.bob during tests.
3. Complete install.sh
The installer must:
1. Validate Node.js.
2. Install dependencies.
3. Build and run all tests before modifying Bob configuration.
4. Copy bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/ to ~/.bob/skills/sdlc-harness/.
5. Copy bob-kit/rules/01-sdlc-harness.md to <project>/.bob/rules/.
6. Safely merge MCP and custom-mode configuration.
7. Remain idempotent and preserve unrelated files.
8. Print accurate next steps.
Update the README so its automated-install description matches actual behavior.
4. Fix the GitLab issue writer
In gitlab-issue-writer.ts and shared types:
- Remove the unsafe labels cast.
- Model GitLab’s create-issue labels payload as a comma-separated string.
- Replace unsupported milestone and assignee strings with:
- milestone_id
- assignee_ids
- Pass these values through on create and update.
- Do not expose arguments that are silently ignored.
- Retain duplicate detection, but document its first-page limitation or paginate through all matching results.
Add tests for:
- Creating with labels, milestone, and assignees.
- Updating labels, milestone, and assignees.
- Add/remove label behavior.
- Close, reopen, and add-note actions.
- Duplicate detection and forced creation.
5. Complete work-item-format validation
Make validation enforce the published standard:
- Epic title maximum: 60 characters.
- Feature title maximum: 60 characters.
- User Story title maximum: 120 characters.
- Bug title maximum: 120 characters.
- Task title maximum: 80 characters.
- User Story titles must contain the complete Connextra structure:
As a/an <role>, I can <action> so that <benefit>.
- Require the documented description sections for Epic, Feature, and Bug.
- Validate Given/When/Then as structured lines, not arbitrary substrings.
- Keep validation results actionable and field-specific.
Add positive and negative tests for every work-item type and every enforced rule.
6. Make the smoke test genuinely end-to-end
Refactor src/smoke.ts or add tests that:
- Create the real MCP server using createServer.
- Connect an MCP SDK client using InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair().
- Call listTools() and verify all four tools are registered.
- Verify every tool exposes a non-empty input schema containing action.
- Invoke each registered tool through the MCP client, not by calling execute() directly.
- Test environment loading:
- Existing environment values win.
- Configurable env-file paths work.
- Missing variables produce a safe error.
- Credential values are never logged.
- Cover all writer actions, not only read operations.
Keep optional live GitLab validation behind SDLC_SMOKE_LIVE=true.
7. Add linting
Add a minimal TypeScript ESLint configuration and an npm run lint script. Remove obsolete suppression comments and the unused dotenv dependency if the custom parser remains.
Acceptance criteria
- npm install succeeds.
- npm run lint succeeds.
- npm run typecheck succeeds.
- npm run build succeeds.
- npm run smoke succeeds.
- MCP listTools() reports four tools with valid, non-empty schemas.
- Representative calls through the MCP transport succeed.
- Invalid existing Bob configuration is never overwritten.
- Re-running the installer produces no duplicate configuration.
- Skill and rule files are installed to their documented locations.
- No credentials or generated files are committed.
- Update to-do.md only after each requirement has been verified.
Scope constraint
Do not implement Section 2B or unrelated refactors. Every changed line must directly support items 7–16 or their verification.

5 | The MCP server builds and its smoke tests pass, but all four registered tools fail when invoked through the real MCP stdio transport.

181 | interface ValidationViolation {
182 |   field: "title" | "description" | "acceptanceCriteria";
183 |   rule: string;
184 |   suggestion?: string;
185 | }
186 | 
187 | function validateItem(
188 |   type: WorkItemType,
189 |   title: string,
190 |   description?: string,
191 |   acceptanceCriteria?: string
192 | ): ValidationViolation[] {
193 |   const template = TEMPLATES[type];
194 |   const violations: ValidationViolation[] = [];
195 | 
196 |   // --- Title checks ---
197 |   if (title.length > 120) {
198 |     violations.push({
199 |       field: "title",
200 |       rule: "Title exceeds 120 characters.",
201 |       suggestion: "Shorten to the core action/outcome.",
202 |     });
203 |   }
204 |   if (type === "User Story" && !title.toLowerCase().startsWith("as a")) {
205 |     violations.push({
206 |       field: "title",
207 |       rule: "User Story titles must follow Connextra format: 'As a <role>, I can...'.",
208 |       suggestion: `Rewrite as: "${template.example.title}"`,
209 |     });
210 |   }
211 |   if (type === "Bug" && !title.includes(":")) {
212 |     violations.push({
213 |       field: "title",
214 |       rule: "Bug titles must follow '<Component>: <symptom>' format.",
215 |       suggestion: `Example: "${template.example.title}"`,
216 |     });
217 |   }
218 | 
219 |   // --- Description checks ---
220 |   if (!description || description.trim().length === 0) {
221 |     violations.push({
222 |       field: "description",
223 |       rule: "Description is empty.",
224 |       suggestion: `Use the ${type} template:\n${template.descriptionStructure}`,
225 |     });
226 |   }
227 | 
228 |   // --- Acceptance criteria checks (User Story and Bug only) ---
229 |   if (type === "User Story" || type === "Bug") {
230 |     if (!acceptanceCriteria || acceptanceCriteria.trim().length === 0) {
231 |       violations.push({
232 |         field: "acceptanceCriteria",
233 |         rule: "Acceptance criteria are required for User Stories and Bugs.",
234 |         suggestion: `Use Given-When-Then format:\n${template.acceptanceCriteriaFormat}`,
235 |       });
236 |     } else {
237 |       const hasGiven = /given/i.test(acceptanceCriteria);
238 |       const hasWhen = /when/i.test(acceptanceCriteria);
239 |       const hasThen = /then/i.test(acceptanceCriteria);
240 |       if (!hasGiven || !hasWhen || !hasThen) {
241 |         violations.push({
242 |           field: "acceptanceCriteria",
243 |           rule: "Acceptance criteria must use Given-When-Then structure.",
244 |           suggestion: `Example:\n${template.acceptanceCriteriaFormat}`,
245 |         });
246 |       }
247 |     }
248 |   }
249 | 
250 |   return violations;
251 | }

+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Connextra validation helper
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+/**
+ * Validates that a User Story title follows the complete Connextra structure:
+ *   As a/an <role>, I can <action> so that <benefit>.
+ *
+ * The validation is case-insensitive and allows optional trailing punctuation.
+ */
+function isValidConnextra(title: string): boolean {
+  // Must start with "As a" or "As an"
+  const lower = title.trim().toLowerCase();
+  if (!lower.startsWith("as a") && !lower.startsWith("as an")) return false;
+  // Must contain ", I can " (comma optional but common)
+  if (!/ i can /i.test(title)) return false;
+  // Must contain " so that " (the benefit clause)
+  if (!/ so that /i.test(title)) return false;
+  return true;
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Given/When/Then structured validation helper
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+/**
+ * Validates that AC contains at least one complete Given/When/Then scenario
+ * as structured lines (each keyword on its own line).
+ *
+ * Accepts both "**Given**" (bold) and "Given" (plain) line starts.
+ */
+function hasStructuredGWT(ac: string): boolean {
+  const lines = ac.split(/\r?\n/).map((l) => l.trim().toLowerCase());
+  const hasGiven = lines.some((l) => l.startsWith("given") || l.startsWith("**given**"));
+  const hasWhen = lines.some((l) => l.startsWith("when") || l.startsWith("**when**"));
+  const hasThen = lines.some((l) => l.startsWith("then") || l.startsWith("**then**"));
+  return hasGiven && hasWhen && hasThen;
+}

+  const lower = title.trim().toLowerCase();
+  if (!lower.startsWith("as a") && !lower.startsWith("as an")) return false;
+  // Must contain ", I can " (comma optional but common)
+  if (!/ i can /i.test(title)) return false;
+  // Must contain " so that " (the benefit clause)
+  if (!/ so that /i.test(title)) return false;
+  return true;
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Given/When/Then structured validation helper
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+/**
+ * Validates that AC contains at least one complete Given/When/Then scenario
+ * as structured lines (each keyword on its own line).
+ *
+ * Accepts both "**Given**" (bold) and "Given" (plain) line starts.
+ */
+function hasStructuredGWT(ac: string): boolean {
+  const lines = ac.split(/\r?\n/).map((l) => l.trim().toLowerCase());
+  const hasGiven = lines.some((l) => l.startsWith("given") || l.startsWith("**given**"));
+  const hasWhen = lines.some((l) => l.startsWith("when") || l.startsWith("**when**"));
+  const hasThen = lines.some((l) => l.startsWith("then") || l.startsWith("**then**"));
+  return hasGiven && hasWhen && hasThen;
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Validation helper
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interface ValidationViolation {
+  field: "title" | "description" | "acceptanceCriteria";
+  rule: string;
+  suggestion?: string;
+}
+
+function validateItem(
+  type: WorkItemType,
+  title: string,
+  description?: string,
+  acceptanceCriteria?: string
+): ValidationViolation[] {
+  const template = TEMPLATES[type];
+  const violations: ValidationViolation[] = [];
+
+  // --- Title checks ---
+  const maxLen = TITLE_MAX_LENGTH[type];
+  if (title.length > maxLen) {
+    violations.push({
+      field: "title",
+      rule: `${type} titles must not exceed ${maxLen} characters (current: ${title.length}).`,
+      suggestion: "Shorten to the core action/outcome.",
+    });
+  }
+
+  if (type === "User Story") {
+    if (!isValidConnextra(title)) {
+      violations.push({
+        field: "title",
+        rule: "User Story titles must follow complete Connextra format: 'As a/an <role>, I can <action> so that <benefit>'.",
+        suggestion: `Example: "${template.example.title}"`,
+      });
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (type === "Bug" && !title.includes(":")) {
+    violations.push({
+      field: "title",
+      rule: "Bug titles must follow '<Component>: <symptom>' format.",
+      suggestion: `Example: "${template.example.title}"`,
+    });
+  }
+
+  // --- Description checks ---
+  if (!description || description.trim().length === 0) {
+    violations.push({
+      field: "description",
+      rule: "Description is empty.",
+      suggestion: `Use the ${type} template:\n${template.descriptionStructure}`,
+    });
+  } else {
+    // Check required sections for types that mandate them
+    const requiredSections = REQUIRED_DESCRIPTION_SECTIONS[type];
+    if (requiredSections) {
+      for (const section of requiredSections) {
+        if (!description.includes(section)) {
+          violations.push({
+            field: "description",
+            rule: `${type} descriptions must include the "${section}" section.`,
+            suggestion: `Add the section heading and its content. Full template:\n${template.descriptionStructure}`,
+          });
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  // --- Acceptance criteria checks (User Story and Bug only) ---
+  if (type === "User Story" || type === "Bug") {
+    if (!acceptanceCriteria || acceptanceCriteria.trim().length === 0) {
+      violations.push({
+        field: "acceptanceCriteria",
+        rule: "Acceptance criteria are required for User Stories and Bugs.",
+        suggestion: `Use Given-When-Then format:\n${template.acceptanceCriteriaFormat}`,
+      });
+    } else if (!hasStructuredGWT(acceptanceCriteria)) {
+      violations.push({
+        field: "acceptanceCriteria",
+        rule: "Acceptance criteria must use structured Given-When-Then format with each keyword on its own line.",
+        suggestion: `Example:\n${template.acceptanceCriteriaFormat}`,
+      });
+    }
+  }
+
+  return violations;
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Tool schema
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+const argsSchema = z.discriminatedUnion("action", [
+  z.object({
+    action: z.literal("get-standard"),
+    type: z.enum(WORK_ITEM_TYPES).optional().describe(
+      "Return standard for a specific type only. Omit for the full standard."
+    ),
+  }),
+  z.object({
+    action: z.literal("get-template"),
+    type: z.enum(WORK_ITEM_TYPES).describe("Work item type to get the template for."),
+  }),
+  z.object({
+    action: z.literal("validate-item"),
+    type: z.enum(WORK_ITEM_TYPES).describe("Work item type to validate against."),
+    title: z.string().describe("Issue title to validate."),
+    description: z.string().optional().describe("Issue description to validate."),
+    acceptanceCriteria: z.string().optional().describe(
+      "Acceptance criteria to validate (relevant for User Story and Bug)."
+    ),
+  }),
+]);
+
+type Args = z.infer<typeof argsSchema>;
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Tool definition
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+export const workItemFormatTool: ToolDefinition<typeof argsSchema> = {
+  name: "work-item-format",
+  description:
+    "Return and validate work item formatting standards. " +
+    "action='get-standard' returns the full formatting standard (optionally filtered to one type). " +
+    "action='get-template' returns the template (structure + example) for a specific type. " +
+    "action='validate-item' checks a title/description/AC against the standard and returns violations with fixes.",
+  argsSchema,
+
+  // Context is not needed (all data is embedded) but must match the signature
+  async execute(args: Args, _context: ToolContext): Promise<unknown> {
+    switch (args.action) {
+      case "get-standard": {
+        if (args.type) {
+          return { standard: TEMPLATES[args.type] };
+        }
+        return { standard: TEMPLATES };
+      }
+
+      case "get-template": {
+        return { template: TEMPLATES[args.type] };
+      }
+
+      case "validate-item": {
+        const violations = validateItem(
+          args.type,
+          args.title,
+          args.description,
+          args.acceptanceCriteria
+        );
+        return {
+          valid: violations.length === 0,
+          violations,
+          template: TEMPLATES[args.type],
+        };
+      }
+    }
+  },
+};

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install.sh — idempotent installer for the sdlc-harness MCP server and Bob skill.
#
# What it does:
#  1. Confirms Node.js ≥18 is available.
#  2. Runs npm install in the mcp-server directory.
#  3. Builds TypeScript (npm run build).
#  4. Runs all tests (npm run smoke) — must pass before touching Bob config.
#  5. Copies bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness/ to ~/.bob/skills/sdlc-harness/.
#  6. Copies bob-kit/rules/01-sdlc-harness.md to <project>/.bob/rules/.
#  7. Merges MCP server and custom-mode configuration into ~/.bob/settings/
#     without overwriting unrelated existing config.
#
# Idempotent: re-running produces no duplicate configuration or copied files.
#
# Usage:
#   bash install.sh
#   bash install.sh /path/to/sdlc-harness   # explicit project root

set -euo pipefail

# Resolve project root (default: grandparent of this script — bob-kit/mcp-server/ → project root)
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="${1:-$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)}"
MCP_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/bob-kit/mcp-server"

echo "sdlc-harness installer"
echo "======================"
echo "Project root : $PROJECT_ROOT"
echo "MCP server   : $MCP_DIR"
echo ""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Node.js version check
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  echo "Error: node is not installed. Install Node.js ≥18 and retry." >&2
  exit 1
fi

NODE_MAJOR=$(node --version | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
if [ "$NODE_MAJOR" -lt 18 ]; then
  echo "Error: Node.js ≥18 required (found $(node --version))." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "✓ Node.js $(node --version)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. npm install
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "Installing dependencies..."
(cd "$MCP_DIR" && npm install --prefer-offline 2>&1)
echo "✓ npm install complete"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Build
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "Building TypeScript..."
(cd "$MCP_DIR" && npm run build 2>&1)
echo "✓ Build complete"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Run tests — gate: must pass before modifying Bob configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "Running smoke tests..."
(cd "$MCP_DIR" && npm run smoke 2>&1)
echo "✓ Smoke tests passed"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Copy skill files to ~/.bob/skills/sdlc-harness/
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "Installing sdlc-harness skill..."
SKILL_SRC="$PROJECT_ROOT/bob-kit/skills/sdlc-harness"
SKILL_DEST="$HOME/.bob/skills/sdlc-harness"

if [ -d "$SKILL_SRC" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$SKILL_DEST"
  cp -r "$SKILL_SRC/." "$SKILL_DEST/"
  echo "✓ Skill copied to $SKILL_DEST"
else
  echo "  ⚠ Skill source not found at $SKILL_SRC — skipping."
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Copy rule file to <project>/.bob/rules/
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "Installing project rule..."
RULE_SRC="$PROJECT_ROOT/bob-kit/rules/01-sdlc-harness.md"
RULE_DEST_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/.bob/rules"

if [ -f "$RULE_SRC" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$RULE_DEST_DIR"
  cp "$RULE_SRC" "$RULE_DEST_DIR/01-sdlc-harness.md"
  echo "✓ Rule copied to $RULE_DEST_DIR/01-sdlc-harness.md"
else
  echo "  ⚠ Rule source not found at $RULE_SRC — skipping."
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Bob config merge (MCP server + custom mode)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "Merging Bob configuration..."
node "$MCP_DIR/merge-bob-config.mjs" "$PROJECT_ROOT"

echo ""
echo "=============================="
echo "Installation complete."
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "  1. Copy .env.example to .env and fill in your GitLab credentials:"
echo "       cp $MCP_DIR/.env.example $PROJECT_ROOT/.env"
echo "  2. Restart Bob to load the sdlc-harness MCP server and mode."
echo "  3. Activate the 'SDLC Harness' mode in Bob to begin governance."
echo "  4. When the GitLab Docker instance is ready, run the live smoke test:"
echo "       SDLC_SMOKE_LIVE=true npm run smoke   (from $MCP_DIR)"

git commit -m "fix(task-10): fix MCP tool registration for discriminated-union schemas

McpServer.registerTool() calls normalizeObjectSchema() which only handles
z.object() schemas with a .shape property. Discriminated unions have no
.shape so the SDK published an empty inputSchema for all four tools, causing
every real MCP call to fail with invalid_union_discriminator.

Fix: switch to the low-level Server API with setRequestHandler, building
MCP-compatible inputSchemas manually via a buildInputSchema() helper that
flattens discriminated unions into a single type:object schema (required by
the MCP spec) with the discriminator as an enum and all per-variant fields
merged as optional properties.

Also add a real MCP transport integration test (testMcpTransportIntegration)
to smoke.ts that spawns dist/index.js via StdioClientTransport, calls
listTools to verify non-empty schemas are published, and invokes
work-item-format through the actual stdio transport. This class of regression
cannot be caught by the previous unit-level tests that call execute() directly.

3 | ## Priority Legend

5 | - **P0** — required for the MVP demo. Nothing else matters until these work end-to-end.

7 | - **P2** — explicitly out of scope for this demo. Listed so it isn't forgotten later, not so it gets built now.
8 | 
9 | ## Scope Decisions
10 | 
11 | - **GitLab hosting:** self-hosted GitLab CE via Docker (confirmed). This is heavier than a hosted alternative — budget real time and RAM for it, and get the smoke test green before building anything on top.
12 | - **Agent tiering:** P0 = Acceptance-criteria drafting, Ambiguity detection, Dependency suggestion, State-transition. P1 = Test-coverage linkage (hardest to seed convincingly with fake data in a live demo — hold back unless the four P0 agents and the demo loop are already solid).
13 | - **Plumbing reuse:** the MCP server skeleton, GitLab REST client, tool-registry pattern, and Bob-config merge/install pattern from the earlier `bob-devops-kit` recreation plan are reused as engineering scaffolding (Section 2A below). Its generic skill set — `backlog-hygiene`, `work-item-optimizer`, `sprint-worker`, `hierarchy-scaffolding`, `code-review`, `formatting-compliance-audit`, `project-researcher` — and its coding-guidelines engine (`guidelines-init/search/status/validate`) solve a **different, adjacent problem** (a general-purpose GitLab coding-assistant kit). 178 | // Validation helper

180 | 
181 | interface ValidationViolation {
182 |   field: "title" | "description" | "acceptanceCriteria";
183 |   rule: string;
184 |   suggestion?: string;
185 | }
186 | 
187 | function validateItem(
188 |   type: WorkItemType,
189 |   title: string,
190 |   description?: string,
191 |   acceptanceCriteria?: string
192 | ): ValidationViolation[] {
193 |   const template = TEMPLATES[type];
194 |   const violations: ValidationViolation[] = [];
195 | 
196 |   // --- Title checks ---
197 |   if (title.length > 120) {
198 |     violations.push({
199 |       field: "title",
200 |       rule: "Title exceeds 120 characters.",
201 |       suggestion: "Shorten to the core action/outcome.",
202 |     });
203 |   }
204 |   if (type === "User Story" && !title.toLowerCase().startsWith("as a")) {
205 |     violations.push({
206 |       field: "title",
207 |       rule: "User Story titles must follow Connextra format: 'As a <role>, I can...'.",
208 |       suggestion: `Rewrite as: "${template.example.title}"`,
209 |     });
210 |   }
211 |   if (type === "Bug" && !title.includes(":")) {
212 |     violations.push({
213 |       field: "title",
214 |       rule: "Bug titles must follow '<Component>: <symptom>' format.",
215 |       suggestion: `Example: "${template.example.title}"`,
216 |     });
217 |   }
218 | 
219 |   // --- Description checks ---
220 |   if (!description || description.trim().length === 0) {
221 |     violations.push({
222 |       field: "description",
223 |       rule: "Description is empty.",
224 |       suggestion: `Use the ${type} template:\n${template.descriptionStructure}`,
225 |     });
226 |   }
227 | 
228 |   // --- Acceptance criteria checks (User Story and Bug only) ---
229 |   if (type === "User Story" || type === "Bug") {
230 |     if (!acceptanceCriteria || acceptanceCriteria.trim().length === 0) {
231 |       violations.push({
232 |         field: "acceptanceCriteria",
233 |         rule: "Acceptance criteria are required for User Stories and Bugs.",
234 |         suggestion: `Use Given-When-Then format:\n${template.acceptanceCriteriaFormat}`,
235 |       });
236 |     } else {
237 |       const hasGiven = /given/i.test(acceptanceCriteria);
238 |       const hasWhen = /when/i.test(acceptanceCriteria);
239 |       const hasThen = /then/i.test(acceptanceCriteria);
240 |       if (!hasGiven || !hasWhen || !hasThen) {
241 |         violations.push({
242 |           field: "acceptanceCriteria",
243 |           rule: "Acceptance criteria must use Given-When-Then structure.",
244 |           suggestion: `Example:\n${template.acceptanceCriteriaFormat}`,
245 |         });
246 |       }
247 |     }
248 |   }
249 | 
250 |   return violations;
251 | }

1 | # WatsonX Model Configuration
2 | 
3 | ## Overview
4 | 
5 | sdlc-harness uses IBM WatsonX AI models via Bob's built-in WatsonX provider.
6 | No extra SDK or HTTP client is required — Bob resolves the model and injects
7 | credentials at inference time using the values already configured in the IDE's
8 | WatsonX provider settings.
9 | 
10 | No model ID, endpoint URL, or API key may appear in any file in this repo.
11 | All credential references below are **names only**; values live in the IDE's
12 | provider settings or a gitignored `.env` file.
13 | 
14 | ---
15 | 
16 | ## Credential injection pattern
17 | 
18 | Bob reads WatsonX credentials from whichever of the following is populated first:
19 | 
20 | 1. **IDE provider settings** — Bob IDE → Settings → Providers → WatsonX:
21 |    fill in `API Key`, `Project ID`, and `Endpoint URL` there. This is the
22 |    preferred approach for the demo machine (single-user, single project).
23 | 
24 | 2. **Environment variables** (fallback, useful in CI or multi-project setups):
25 | 
26 |    | Variable | Purpose |
27 |    |---|---|
28 |    | `WATSONX_API_KEY` | IAM API key for the WatsonX instance |
29 |    | `WATSONX_PROJECT_ID` | WatsonX project / space ID |
30 |    | `WATSONX_URL` | WatsonX inference endpoint (region-specific) |
31 | 
32 |    These may be set in the demo machine's shell profile or in a gitignored
33 |    `.env` file at the repo root. Never commit values.
34 | 
35 | 3. **`.env` file path** — if Bob supports a `WATSONX_ENV_FILE` pointer, set
36 |    it to the absolute path of a gitignored env file (same pattern as
37 |    `SOPHIE_ENV_FILE` in the sophie-tools MCP server).
38 | 
39 | `.gitignore` and `.bobignore` both block `*.env*` files. Verify before
40 | running the demo.
41 | 
42 | ---
43 | 
44 | ## Model selection rationale
45 | 
46 | | Agent role | Selected model | Rationale |
47 | |---|---|---|
48 | | **Acceptance-criteria drafting** | `ibm/granite-3-3-8b-instruct` | Instruction-following strength; 128 k context fits a full-issue thread plus template. Fast enough for interactive use (developer waiting for a draft). |
49 | | **Ambiguity detection** | `ibm/granite-3-3-8b-instruct` | Same model; classifier-style reasoning over short description text. The 8 B parameter count keeps latency low for repeated single-issue calls. |
50 | | **Dependency suggestion** | `ibm/granite-3-3-8b-instruct` (128 k window) | Needs to reason over many open issues simultaneously. The 128 k context window lets the full backlog (≤ 200 issues at ~300 tokens each) fit in one call. |
51 | | **State-transition suggestion** | `ibm/granite-3-3-8b-instruct` | Lightweight signal-matching task (MR merged → suggest "In Review"). No long-context requirement; fast response is more important than recall depth. |
52 | | **P1 — Test-coverage linkage** | `ibm/granite-3-3-8b-instruct` | Cross-referencing issue text against test-file names and assertions. 128 k window accommodates a reasonably large test suite alongside the issue backlog. |
53 | 
54 | All roles use the same model family, which simplifies the demo setup (one
55 | model configured → all agents work). The 8B instruct variant balances
56 | reasoning quality against inference latency for interactive governance loops.
57 | 
58 | If a larger model is available on the demo WatsonX instance, swap in
59 | `ibm/granite-3-8b-instruct` or the latest Granite 3.x checkpoint; the
60 | `customInstructions` in `custom_modes.yaml` reference the model by name so the
61 | switch requires only a one-line edit there.
62 | 
63 | ---
64 | 
65 | ## Wiring in `custom_modes.yaml`
66 | 
67 | The `sdlc-harness` mode's `customInstructions` block already states:
68 | 
69 | ```
70 | WatsonX model in use: ibm/granite-3-3-8b-instruct via Bob's configured provider.
71 | For long-context tasks (full-backlog audit, dependency graph) prefer
72 | ibm/granite-3-3-8b-instruct with a 128k context window.
73 | ```
74 | 
75 | This is the only place the model name is recorded in config. Bob reads it as a
76 | hint at inference time. To change the model for the whole skill, update that
77 | one line — no other files need editing.
78 | 
79 | ---
80 | 
81 | ## Demo machine setup checklist
82 | 
83 | 1. Open Bob IDE → Settings → Providers → WatsonX.
